survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports descriptive and comparative results from PISA 2022 for Denmark, based on the OECD PISA 2022 Database. The underlying PISA design is a complex, stratified sampling of schools and students, and OECD typically uses sampling weights to produce population-representative estimates for each country. The factsheet does not specify the exact weight variable name (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or whether replicate weights were used, so the precise weighting implementation cannot be confirmed from the provided text. Plausible values are used for cognitive achievement reporting in PISA; however, the factsheet does not document the PV combining procedure or missing-data handling details, so analysts should consult the PISA 2022 technical documentation/reader’s guide for the exact procedures.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values handling is not applicable here because this document is a country factsheet that summarizes published PISA results (means, trends, and proficiency-level shares) rather than reporting an original student-level modeling workflow with explicit PV procedures. This is a reporting/coverage limitation typical of high-level dissemination products rather than a methodological transparency gap for an original analysis.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic sample reported in the factsheet is the set of students in Denmark who completed the PISA 2022 assessment in mathematics, reading, or science (two-hour subject tests with different booklets assigned to different students). The factsheet does not provide additional inclusion/exclusion rules beyond noting that, due to COVID-19-related exceptional circumstances, Denmark excluded more students than in 2018 and that many exclusions were linked to dyslexia accommodations not available in PISA.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Denmark factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students in Denmark performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how results changed over time. It reports mean performance trends (down in mathematics and reading from 2018 to 2022; about stable in science), proficiency-level distributions (e.g., shares at Level 2+ and Level 5/6), and within-country gaps by socio-economic status and gender. It also highlights that PISA 2022 was delayed to 2022 from 2021 due to COVID-19, and that Denmark excluded more students than in 2018, with many exclusions related to dyslexia accommodations not available in PISA. The factsheet provides comparative benchmarks against the OECD average and selected comparison countries, but it does not present an original ML modeling pipeline, PV-combining method, or missing-data procedure in the text provided.
